text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel, on an official visit to Turkey, rules out the possibility of Turkey's becoming a full member of European Union (EU) in the short run.

- Tansu Ciller, leader of the conservative coalition partner, is gearing up to ask Islamist premier Necmettin Erbakan to allow her to take her turn as prime minister this year, a year ahead of schedule. The aim would be to avoid any further trouble arising from Islamist-secularist tensions.

- Senior Islamist deputy Oguzhan Asilturk denies that Prime Minister Erbakan signed a declaration of the military-dominated National Security Council (MGK) to combat Islamist activisim. Asilturk said the declaration was not binding for any ministers.

- An opinion poll reveals that 72.6 percent of Turks support eight years of uniterrupted compulsory education, which the Islamists oppose on the grounds that this will effectively close down the middle section of religious schools.
- The strictly securalist Turkish army has recently became more influential in Turkish foreign policy.
- The MGK will discuss Islamist threats against the secular state at its meeting on March 31.
- Turkey will lift anti-damping taxes on cotton thread by March 28. This opens the door to exporting Turkish cotton thread to the European Union.
- A General Staff report reveals that the Incirlik air base in southern Turkey, used by a U.S.-allied airforce to protect Iraqi Kurds, is being used to dump chemical waste.
